If the AI-tell hit recurs on consecutive nights, add the matched phrase to the banned list in the script prompt.

The short script was expanded to 3371 words, against a 3400 target

The first draft came in at 2692 words, below the 3400 target, and was sent back for up to two expand passes. The episode that shipped has 3371 words. The gap to target is the number to watch, not the expansion itself: the pipeline accepted a script that still falls short of what it asked for.

The first script draft named Meta and Moment, neither of which appears in the week's commits, so the draft failed. The retry aired with upstream changes in place of the failed draft. The listener hears a script that was regenerated, and the only record of the discarded version is this degradation entry.

The source of the hallucinated names is not in the facts. Look at what the script step receives as its commit context before the next run.

Three TTS takes came back short and one retry stayed short

Three audio segments returned shorter than their word counts predicted. Each was retried once. One retry was still short, and the longer of the two takes was kept, so no audio was dropped from the episode.

The remaining two were recovered by the retry. Only the one that stayed short is still a risk, and it is the take that was kept, so listen to that segment before assuming the episode is clean.

What happened

The script ran short, then was expanded to 3575 words

The first script draft came in at 2585 words against a 3400-word target, so it was sent back for up to two expand passes. The shipped script is 3575 words. Expansion closed the gap but the first draft was not usable as written, and the expand passes are the reason the script cost what it did. The first draft missed its target by a wide margin; the review's job is to say that plainly rather than let the shipped number hide it.

The roundup pool is larger than one segment can air by design: 61 stories were cut by the airtime budget. Citation alignment is the weaker signal here. Only 8 of 18 roundup citations matched, and 2 of 5 deep-dive citations matched. Those ratios should be checked against the sources before the next run is trusted on attribution.

Twelve of 24 candidates had no research record

Election research found nothing for 12 of the 24 candidates on the ballot: Laura Zimmerman, Nicole Berreth, Greg Jeannotte, Charlene Hays, Cianna O'Connor, Rafiullah Sahibzada, Billie Sheridan, Whitney Spearing, Nathan Wiebe, Kayla Zaruk, Ruth Lloyd and Michael Franklin. The debate question asks whether re-election reflects a record in office or an inherited name, and half the field has no record the script could draw on. Any segment that discusses those candidates is working from the name alone.

Change the candidate research step to flag unresolved names for a second search pass before the script is written, not after.

One short TTS take, and the longer take was kept

One TTS take came back shorter than its word count predicted, and the retry was also short. The longer of the two takes was kept, so the episode itself is complete; the short retry is the only evidence of the problem.

The first script draft came in at 3163 words against a target of 3400. The pipeline sent it back for up to two expand passes, and the script that shipped is 3515 words. One text-to-speech take returned shorter than its word count predicts. Each such take is retried once, and this was the only one tonight. The facts record the retry, not whether the retried take came back at full length, so treat the audio at that point as unverified.

Two of the four deep-dive sources are a local election story and a theme-park death, and the debate question about who holds responsibility for outdoor safety decisions sits awkwardly against both. Check the two unmatched deep-dive citations against their source articles before the next run, since the mismatch may be in the extraction step rather than the script.

65 roundup stories were cut by the airtime budget

The roundup pool held more stories than one segment can air, so 65 were dropped by the airtime budget set in NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT. This is by design, and a dropped story can resurface on a day when it fits the debate better.
